## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="f09-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- f09-ideas:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<dl class="lx-ideas"><dt>Carriers to sectors</dt><dd>A city buys gas, fuels and electricity, and uses them in buildings, transport and industry; buildings take the most, 3,994 GWh.</dd><dt>Useful and lost</dt><dd>Engines lose most of their fuel as heat: transport turns 30% of what it takes in into motion.</dd><dt>The power sector</dt><dd>Prairie City makes 0.9% of its electricity; its accounting starts where the regional grid's power enters its wires.</dd><dt>Who decides</dt><dd>Typically the state regulator sets utility rates, federal rules set equipment standards and interstate markets, the city sets codes and permits, and owners choose their equipment.</dd><dt>Typical, not universal</dt><dd>A city that owns its utility sets its own rates; states differ in codes and in how their utilities are organised.</dd></dl>
<!-- f09-ideas:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Where a city's count starts</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **[Final energy]{.lx-term term="final-energy"}** is what the city buys at the meter or the pump; [useful energy]{.lx-term term="useful-energy"} is the warmth, motion and light it gets.
- **A convention.** For appliances, lights and computers the electricity delivered counts as useful; for heat and vehicles, the heat or motion delivered.
- **The boundary.** Power plants on the regional grid are outside the city: their losses appear in a regional or national count, not here.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Who decides, in a little more detail</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Rates.** An investor-owned utility asks its state commission to change rates; the commission reviews its costs and approves the rates and terms.
- **Supply.** In states without retail competition, as in Kansas, utilities may build, own and run power plants; states with retail competition leave generation to competing suppliers.
- **The grid.** A regional operator such as SPP runs the bulk grid and the wholesale market under FERC's rules.
- **Codes.** The U.S. has no national energy code: states or local governments adopt one, and local permit offices enforce it.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What this lesson leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>Emissions from each flow, and how a city counts them.</li>
<li>Hours and seasons: a year's flows hide the coldest evening.</li>
<li>Costs and who pays them.</li>
<li>Rules outside the U.S., and the details of any one state's law.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

Fact where the city owns its utility.</p></details></div><div class="lx-qq" data-id="cars" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Most of the energy a car burns moves the car.”</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. <p class="lx-hint">Who decides what (typical U.S. practice):</p><ul><li>U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Electricity Delivery and Energy Reliability. <a href="https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2015/12/f28/united-states-electricity-industry-primer.pdf">United States Electricity Industry Primer (DOE/OE-0017)</a>. The Commission's Role (no link). Undated; read 6 November 2026. The Utilities Division establishes and regulates rates for public utilities; the KCC does not regulate most electric cooperatives or municipalities.</li><li>Kansas Corporation Commission staff. Rate Study (no link). Undated (about January 2019); read 6 November 2026. P. 2: each electric utility builds an integrated system to generate, transmit and distribute electricity in its service territory.</li><li>U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy. <a href="https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=40913">Investor-owned utilities served 72% of U.S. electricity customers in 2017</a>. 15 August 2019; data for 2017. Local electric utilities operate the distribution system that connects homes and businesses to the grid; utilities plan for future power needs.</li><li>Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. <a href="https://www.ferc.gov/what-ferc-does">What FERC Does</a>. Updated 18 June 2025. Regulates the transmission and wholesale sale of electricity in interstate commerce, and interstate natural gas pipelines; does not regulate retail sales to consumers.</li><li>U.S. Department of Energy. <a href="https://www.energy.gov/cmei/buildings/appliance-and-equipment-standards-program">Appliance and Equipment Standards Program</a>. Updated 15 May 2026.
